fields.meta_description: Build an identity verification form that collects ID details and photos, queues every case for review, and saves each decision to your database.
fields.h1: Build an Identity Verification Form With ID Review
fields.hero_description: Build an identity verification form that reads uploaded IDs into fields and sends each case to a reviewer you choose.
fields.features_heading: What Applicants Submit and Reviewers Decide
fields.features_subheading: Applicants see the first three parts. Reviewers work in the next two, and the sixth is the code behind all of them.
fields.feature_1:
Four identity details, each its own field

The form asks for legal name, date of birth, home address, and an ID number as separate required fields. The birth date field takes only a real date, never a typed sentence.
fields.feature_2:
Both sides of the ID, read into fields

Applicants upload the front and back of a photo ID. The app reads the name, date of birth, and expiry date into fields, and a field it reads with low confidence goes to a person.
fields.feature_3:
A signed declaration on the last screen

The final screen asks applicants to confirm that every detail is true and to sign with a finger or a mouse. The signature is saved with the case, beside the uploads it covers.
fields.feature_4:
Approve, reject, or ask for a new photo

Reviewers open each case next to its ID images and pick one of those three outcomes. The app records who decided, when, and why, on the same database row as the case itself.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for cases nobody has opened

A new case posts to a Slack channel or reaches the reviewer by email. A case that stays open past your deadline sends its reviewer a reminder, then escalates to the team lead.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, in your repository

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The form can then sit beside the rest of your onboarding code, with each later change reviewed as a pull request.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams That Check an ID First
fields.tab_content_1:
Kwame checks the one field the app was unsure of

Odette Varga applies for a loan with Tallgrass Lending and uploads both sides of her driver's license. The app reads 4 fields from it into her application: name, date of birth, license number, and address. The address comes back with low confidence, and it waits for reviewer Kwame Ellison while the other 3 fill in.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 2 of 2 IDs seen, the signing step opens

Rafael Duarte fills in the form at home before closing on 41 Fenwick Road with Copperline Title. At the closing table, closer Hana Lindqvist holds his passport and driver's license and marks each as seen in person. With 2 of 2 IDs marked, the app opens the signing step for the closing documents.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three requests move on and an expired one returns

Quillstack's support team takes account recovery requests through the form, each with the account email and a photo ID. Four requests came in this morning. Three go to an agent. Will Hargrove's driver's license expired in August, and his request goes back to him with a note asking for a current ID.
fields.tab_content_4:
Slack gets her enrollment name with the request

Marisol Quintero asks Calloway College for a transcript and uploads her driver's license. She enrolled as Marisol Pike, and the form asks for that name as well. The registrar team's Slack channel gets the request with both names and her class year, 2014, and staff search the student records under Pike.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Identity Verification Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an identity verification form that collects ID details, routes each case to a reviewer, and records the decision.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what a case needs
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the confidence bar for ID readings
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Require a reason on every rejection
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what your process needs before a case can close: the identity fields, the documents you accept, and what makes an upload unusable. If counsel or a regulator sets that list, copy their wording. The list becomes your prompt in the next step.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Type in plain English what applicants fill in, what they upload, and who reviews the result. Emergent builds the form, the review screen, and a database table for every case. Prompt again whenever a field or a rule needs to change.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose which fields the app reads from each uploaded ID. Then pick the confidence level below which a reading goes to a person. Start strict, and loosen it once a week of real cases shows where the readings hold up.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give reviewers their three buttons and make the reason field mandatory on a rejection. When a reviewer asks for a new photo, have the app email the applicant a link back to the same case, with the earlier answers still filled in.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick who hears about a new case
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send each new case to a Slack channel or to one reviewer by email. Add a reminder for any case still open after 2 days, and an escalation to the team lead at 4 days. Name the lead in the prompt, not a shared inbox.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with three sample cases
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one clean case, one with a blurry photo, and one with an expired ID. Open the database afterward and confirm that each row holds the uploads, the readings, and the reviewer's decision, with the reason on the rejected one.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish the form and send the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the form on a custom domain; Emergent includes custom domains, and they use credits. Send the link from the email or account page where applicants start, and take down any old PDF version so nobody fills in the wrong one.

faq_plan.q: What is the identity verification form?
faq_plan.ref: What is the identity verification form?

prov.original: What is the identity verification form?

faq_plan.a: It is a form that collects what an organization needs to confirm you are the person you claim to be: legal name, date of birth, address, an ID number, and a copy of a photo ID. Staff compare those details with the ID and with their own records before they act on your request.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an identity verification form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the identity fields, the ID uploads, who reviews each case, and what happens after approval. Emergent builds identity verification forms with the review screen and the database behind them. Run two test cases through yours before real applicants get the link.

faq_plan.q: Where can I get an identity verification form?
faq_plan.ref: where can i get an identity verification form
faq_plan.a: From the organization that asked you for one. Use the version it gives you, because its fields match its own records, and a lookalike from another site can ask for the wrong details. If the organization sends its identity verification form as a PDF, fill in that file. If you are the one asking, you can build your own on Emergent with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: What is a land title identity verification form?
faq_plan.ref: what is a land title identity verification form
faq_plan.a: In Australia, it is the Land Title Verification of Identity Form, which your conveyancing practitioner gives you to complete. Once your identity check is done at Australia Post, the post office can send your information on to the practitioner. If you are setting up a US closing instead, keep bank details off the identity form and collect them on a separate ACH form.

faq_plan.q: What information goes on a KYC form?
faq_plan.a: For a US bank, at least four details before an account opens: name, date of birth, address, and an identification number, under the customer identification rule in 31 CFR 1020.220. The same rule lists documents a bank can check them against, such as unexpired government-issued photo ID like a driver's license or passport. Your counsel decides what else your KYC form needs.

faq_plan.q: Is there an identity verification form template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but any template fixes someone else's fields and someone else's review steps. Start from your own list instead: the details you need, the documents you accept, and who makes the call. Emergent turns that list into the form and its review queue from one description, so nothing on it is left over from another company's process.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free identity verification form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing, so you can put a free identity verification form live and test it with real applicants before you pay for anything. The same tier works for lighter jobs, such as a t shirt order form for a club.

faq_plan.q: How to fill out land title identity verification form?
faq_plan.ref: how to fill out land title identity verification form
faq_plan.a: Fill in your details but leave the signature blank. Australia Post's instructions say not to sign the form, because an Australia Post Identity Verifier must witness your signature. Bring two original and current Category 1 documents, and check before you go that all of them show matching personal information.

faq_plan.q: Which identity verification form does a bank ask for?
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: Each bank uses its own, tied to the written customer identification program that 31 CFR 1020.220 requires every US bank to fit to its size and type of business. Beyond your ID, the bank can compare what you enter with records from a consumer reporting agency or a public database. The rule also requires it to tell you that it is asking for this information to verify your identity.

faq_plan.q: What is notarized identity verification form?
faq_plan.ref: what is notarized identity verification form
faq_plan.a: It is an identity form you sign in front of a notary, who confirms you are the person named on it. California's rule, for example, bars a notary from taking an acknowledgment without satisfactory evidence that the signer is the individual described in the document. Card details for the same request go on a separate credit card authorization form.

plan.angle: The top 10 is one organization's form at a time (Delta, NY State of Health, WA DOH, APS, JHU, the IRS) plus two template pages; none shows how an organization runs identity checks behind its own form. This page is for the team that needs its own KYC-style intake: four identity details as fields, both sides of a photo ID read into the case, a signed declaration, and a reviewer who approves, rejects or asks again, with every case a row in a database the team owns. It makes no claim that the form verifies identity or meets any rule; the FAQ answers the issuer-specific searches (land title, notarized, a bank's own form) from primary sources.
